content:
Quick comments for now. I'll do a more detailed review once the points below have been addressed.

Goal
* Typo: instable => unstable

* level 2 add plates and tiles: I understand that you're planning a Level 2 version of the puzzle. Could you briefly explain what additional mechanics this introduces? An example test case would be helpful.

Input
* Typo: numbr => number

* Please change '" " separated' to 'space-separated'.

* Please remove "First is the brickName, second is the brickSize, next is the brickColor and finally the brickCount", and then list the fields individually like this:

• [[brickName]] (string): [description]
• [[brickSize]] (integer): [description]
• [[brickColor]] (string): [description]
• [[brickCount]] (integer): [description]

* For [[H]] and [[W]], please change "Line" to "Next line".

* Please change "[[N]] next" and "[[H]] next" to "Next [[N]]" and "Next [[H]]" respectively.

Constraints
* Please move the current constraint to the Output section, since it describes the required output order.

* Please write one constraint for each input variable.

Stub generator
* Please use the same variable names as those defined in the Input section.

Cases
* In Pacman (Test 5) and Pacman (Validator 5), one brick type has [[brickCount]] = 0. Is it necessary to cover this scenario?

* The following validator cases are identical to their corresponding test cases:
  • Black & white (Test 4) and Black & white (Validator 4)
  • Pacman (Test 5) and Pacman (Validator 5)
  Please revise the validators so that they cover the same scenario as the corresponding tests but with slightly different inputs and outputs.

* Please remove the trailing newlines from the input for:
  • Simple (Test 1)
  • Pacman (Validator 5)

* Please remove the trailing newlines from the output for:
  • Simple (Test 1)
  • Pyramid (Test 2)
  • Pyramid (Validator 2)
  • Battlements (Test 3)
  • Battlements (Validator 3)
  • Black & white (Test 4)
  • Black & white (Validator 4)

Thanks.

>All bricks are 1 large

What is 1 large? It is a bit confusing reading that at the beginning of the blurb.
Ok, depth is better I presume.
